key_themes: Broadcom earnings disappoint on AI chip outlook, triggering $1T semiconductor sector sell-off
Meta considers multi-billion-dollar secondary stock offering to fund AI capex, weighing on mega-cap tech
Quantinuum Nasdaq IPO debut concentrates quantum capital, pressuring Rigetti, D-Wave, and IonQ

stocks.discussion_driver: Broadcom reported a strong fiscal Q2 2026 beat ($22.19B revenue, $2.44 EPS adj.) with AI chip revenue up 143% YoY, but the stock cratered ~13% because CEO Hock Tan merely reiterated the $100B FY27 AI revenue target rather than raising it, and Q3 AI guidance of $16B missed the Street's $17.2B estimate. The disappointment triggered one of the largest post-earnings drops in recent megacap history, wiping ~$320B in market cap and sparking a broad $1T semiconductor sector selloff.
bull_case: AI semiconductor revenue doubled YoY to $10.8B in Q2 and management guided Q3 AI revenue to $16B (200%+ YoY growth), demonstrating sustained hyperscaler demand for Broadcom's custom AI chips (XPUs).
Strong Buy consensus from 47+ analysts with an average price target of ~$511, implying ~29% upside; multiple firms raised targets post-earnings, signaling the selloff is an overreaction.
bear_case: Broadcom reiterated — but did not raise — its full-year $100B AI chip revenue target for FY2027, and Q3 AI guidance of $16B missed analyst expectations of $17.2B, introducing meaningful near-term uncertainty.
Trailing P/E of ~94 is 113% above AVGO's 10-year median of ~44, leaving limited margin of safety if AI growth momentum stalls or hyperscaler capex slows.

stocks.discussion_driver: NVDA dropped ~6.2% on June 5, 2026 as Broadcom's fiscal Q2 earnings projected Q3 AI chip revenue of $16B vs. street estimates of $17.2B and left FY2027 guidance unchanged at $100B, disappointing investors who expected a raise. This triggered the broadest semiconductor sector selloff since March 2020, erasing ~$923B in combined semiconductor market cap in a single session; NVIDIA alone lost ~$280B and its market cap briefly fell below the $5 trillion threshold.
bull_case: AI infrastructure supercycle remains intact — NVIDIA's data center GPU dominance (H100/B100/B200 platforms) gives it unrivaled pricing power and a multi-year backlog as hyperscalers accelerate capital expenditures.
Trailing P/E of ~31x is well below NVDA's 20-year average of 55x and forward P/E of ~22x, suggesting strong valuation support; RSI near 33 signals a potential oversold rebound entry point.
bear_case: Broadcom's soft Q3 AI chip revenue guidance signals that custom ASIC alternatives may be eroding NVIDIA's TAM, dampening the AI chip growth narrative that has driven NVDA's premium valuation.

NVDA is down ~12% from its May 14 all-time high of $236.54 and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index posted its worst single-day drop since March 2020 (-10.3%), with broader sector de-rating risk remaining elevated.

stocks.discussion_driver: ARM fell ~7% on June 5, 2026 as Broadcom's fiscal Q2 earnings failed to raise its full-year AI semiconductor guidance (reiterating $100B+ for FY2027), sending Broadcom shares down ~13% and triggering a broad semiconductor sector sell-off. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 5–6%+ on the day; ARM was particularly hard-hit given its extreme valuation (P/E ~479) and a YTD rally of 270%+ entering June, making it a prime target for profit-taking.
bull_case: ARM's AGI CPU platform has secured over $2 billion in committed customer demand for FY2027–FY2028, with data center royalty revenue more than doubling YoY in Q4 FY2026, establishing ARM as the default architecture for AI inference.
Armv9 royalty ramp is still in early innings with royalty rates 2x those of Armv8; rising agentic-AI CPU demand from Oracle and ByteDance expands the total addressable market significantly.
bear_case: ARM trades at a trailing P/E of ~479 and forward P/E of ~190, leaving essentially zero margin for error — even a modest earnings miss could trigger a severe de-rating from current extreme valuation levels.

RISC-V represents a growing open-source architectural threat to ARM's licensing model, and ARM's move into direct chip competition (AGI CPU) risks alienating existing licensees who underwrite the royalty stream.

stocks.discussion_driver: MU dropped ~17% over two sessions (June 4–5, 2026) following Broadcom's Q2 earnings report, in which AI chip revenue guidance came in ~$1.2B below consensus and Broadcom declined to raise its full-year AI revenue target. Micron was particularly hard-hit given its ~$1 trillion market cap milestone had just been reached and its stock had climbed ~70% YTD; as the leading HBM supplier to AI accelerator makers, MU trades in close sympathy with AI capex sentiment.
bull_case: Micron is a critical supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI accelerators; structural demand from data center AI buildout remains intact despite the near-term sentiment reset.

Forward P/E of ~9.77 is deeply discounted relative to trailing P/E of ~46, reflecting strong expected earnings growth — 39 of 40 analysts still rate the stock Buy or Strong Buy with targets averaging ~$860.
bear_case: Broadcom's AI chip revenue guidance miss signals potential cooling in AI capex, which directly threatens HBM/DRAM demand that drives Micron's premium valuation.

RSI reached 90 on June 1 — historically rare overbought territory — and the stock had surged ~70% in 2026 before the selloff, leaving significant downside risk if AI spending growth disappoints further.

stocks.discussion_driver: On June 5, 2026, Bloomberg and the Financial Times reported that Meta Platforms is considering raising tens of billions of dollars in new equity — inspired by Alphabet's successful $85B stock sale — to help fund up to $145B in AI infrastructure capex through 2026. Meta has not yet hired banks and may not proceed, but the dilution risk triggered a ~6–7% intraday selloff; the capex target of $145B (up from a prior $115–135B range) reflects soaring AI compute costs as Zuckerberg pursues 'personal superintelligence' across Meta's platforms.
bull_case: Analyst consensus is Strong Buy with average price target of ~$834, implying 41%+ upside from June 5 close; Meta's AI monetization model (ad targeting, Llama integration) is seen as among the most advanced of any hyperscaler.

Meta's $145B capex plan signals aggressive AI infrastructure buildout that could entrench competitive moats in social media, AR/VR, and AI assistants, with revenue growth projected to remain robust through 2027.
bear_case: A potential secondary equity offering worth tens of billions of dollars would be dilutive to existing shareholders; equity raises of this scale typically compress near-term EPS and signal concern about cash generation relative to capex ambitions.

The stock is ~26% below its 52-week high of $796.25 (August 2025), and RSI of ~41.6 reflects neutral-to-weak momentum; the stock has failed to recapture its prior peak despite strong Q1 2026 earnings.
